turns.answer_text:
The closest-looking route in the data is to stay in the high-Tc cuprate region: high oxygen fraction, substantial Cu, and Ba/Y-type cations, while avoiding suppressing substitutions such as Zn, Pr, Fe, Ni, etc.

The training data show Y/Ba/Cu/O compositions rising into the 50–60 K range when oxygenated, but with Zn/Ca/La/Pr disorder or nonoptimal stoichiometry. A natural undoped, fully oxygenated extrapolation is the well-known Y–Ba–Cu–O stoichiometry:

\[
\mathrm{Y_1Ba_2Cu_3O_7}
\]

Normalized to element fractions, total atoms \(=1+2+3+7=13\):

- O = 7/13 = 0.538462  
- Cu = 3/13 = 0.230769  
- Ba = 2/13 = 0.153846  
- Y = 1/13 = 0.076923  

All other listed elements are set to zero.
